page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.8-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance is powered by an Ampere AmpereOne-M processor running at a base clock speed of 3.6 GHz. It is provisioned with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, maintaining a single-thread-per-core configuration that prevents core execution sharing between virtual threads. Memory capacity is allocated at 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of system memory per core.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage, meaning persistent data storage must be attached via remote block volumes. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs present on the platform. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address directly assigned to the virtual machine interface.

Because each core is fully dedicated with single-threaded execution, the architecture offers consistent performance profiles free from simultaneous multithreading (SMT) interference. The 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio makes VM.Standard.A4.Flex.8-64 cost-efficient for scale-out applications, microservices, continuous integration and build pipelines, web application serving, and backend services optimized for the ARM64 instruction set.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.8-64 is an ARM64 general-purpose instance powered by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor running at 3.6 GHz. The server provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs without hardware hyperthreading, ensuring predictable single-thread execution without contention. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, matching an industry-standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage, requiring external block storage volumes for persistent data, and does not contain discrete GPU hardware accelerators. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The balanced hardware footprint offers efficient resource allocation for multi-threaded services, build servers, web application backends, container orchestration nodes, and distributed microservices tailored to ARM-based enterprise cloud environments.
